questions.q_en: Select the option with the correct use of future tense.
options_en: If you worked hard in the same manner, you will soon achieve success.
If you had work hard in the same manner, you will soon achieve success.
If you have work hard in the same manner, you will soon achieve success.
If you work hard in the same manner, you will soon achieve success.
questions.solution_en:
Option 4 uses the first conditional ("If + present simple, will + base verb"), which is correct for describing a likely future outcome based on a present condition. The structure is "If you work hard" (present simple) followed by "you will achieve success" (future simple).

Option 1: If you worked hard: Uses past simple ("worked"), which implies an unreal or hypothetical situation (second conditional), not a future likelihoo4.

Option 2: If you had work hard: Incorrect verb form ("had work" should be "had worked") and uses the third conditional for past unreal situations, not future.

Option 3: If you have work hard: Incorrect verb form ("have work" should be "have worked") and doesn't align with future tense structure.

Hence, the correct answer is option (4).

Delilah watched smiling as this year's batch of fresh students entered into her classroom. Once all six children were in the room, the door closed with a small snap. Catherine and Isabella, names Delilah knew from the files she had studied carefully in the weeks before the start of the semester, looked around suspiciously but quickly decided that the noise posed no threat. After all they didn't know that the door had closed of its own accord. Delilah gestured towards the six cushioned chairs each behind a sizeable desk and the children took their seats, some more reluctantly than others. Catherine immediately slouched in her chair and crossed her arms in defiance. Ian rested his head lazily in one hand with elbows on the desk. The rest were still nervous about making a bad impression and sat upright, perfectly still. It was a difficult day for the children.

Each child had been tracked and contacted as soon as they turned fourteen. Some were easy to find. Only Catherine had proven difficult but the recruitment department had found her anyway and brought her here, as planned, in time for school. The Owl Academy was a unique, elite school for a very select group of students but Delilah doubted that anyone had heard of it before. Ian's father was very rich and was possibly one of the many wealthy individuals who had heard of the school and tried to buy their child a place. No one knew what the school taught exactly or what its methods were, the only thing that those in the know were certain of was that every child who had ever gone there had grown to be highly successful in whatever field they chose. But no one could buy their way into Owl Academy. There was no application process, no entrance exams, and no open days. Through a process known only to higher administration, students were selected from across the country and invited to attend. Few refused from time to time. Very few invitations were sent each year. This year, all six invitations had been accepted.

How many students got admission into the Owl Academy in the current year?
questions.solution_en:
The last sentence of the second paragraph clearly mentions that "This year, all six invitations had been accepted". So, a total of six students got admission into the Owl Academy this year.

Hence, option (b) is the correct answer.

Correct sentence would be - 'The global community agrees that this would be the best way of preventing countries from getting into trade wars, which had pushed the global economy into the depression of the 1930s.'

Answer is option (c).

Petrified wood is type of fossilised wood that exhibits the original details of the wood.
options_en: Petrified wood is the type of fossilised wood that exhibits a original details of the wood.
A petrified wood is type of fossilised wood that exhibits an original details of the wood.
The petrified wood is the type of fossilised wood that exhibits a original details of the wood.
Petrified wood is a type of fossilised wood that exhibits the original details of the wood.
questions.solution_en:
· Original sentence: "Petrified wood is type of fossilised wood that exhibits the original details of the wood."

· Error: Missing article "a" before "type," making it grammatically incomplete ("is type" should be "is a type").

· Option 1: "Petrified wood is the type.. a original details" - Incorrect; "a original" should be "the original" (article mismatch).

· Option 2: "A petrified wood is type.. an original details" - Incorrect; "a petrified wood" is wrong (no article needed before "petrified wood" as a general noun), and "an original details" is ungrammatical ("details" is plural, needs "the original").

· Option 3: "The petrified wood is the type.. a original details" - Incorrect; "the petrified wood" implies a specific piece (not general), and "a original details" is wrong.

· Option 4: "Petrified wood is a type of fossilised wood that exhibits the original details of the wood" - Correct; adds "a" before "type" and uses "the original details" appropriately for a general statement.

Thus, option 4 is the correct sentence.

questions.solution_en:
'From' [preposition] is used to refer to the place where someone or something starts or originates. We can use 'to' [as a preposition] to indicate a destination or direction. 'From' requires 'to' after it in order to complete the thought. Example- I've visited many cities in Asia, from Hong Kong, Beijing, Tokyo to Taipei.

'Too' [adverb] and 'form' [verb/noun] are not prepositions and are irrelevant here.

Hence, option (c) is correct.

Note:

A Preposition is a word placed before a noun or a pronoun or a noun equivalent (pronoun, adverb, gerund, infinitive, adverbial clause, or any clause that can be used as the object of the preposition) and shows a relationship in space or time or a logical relationship between two or more people, places, or things in a sentence.

Examples

1) The teacher scolded the child for being late.

2) We're going to a party.

· The noun/pronoun which is used with a preposition is called its Object.

questions.q_en:
Select the most appropriate phrasal verb to fill in the blank.

The driver very subtly ____ the traffic violation he committed.
questions.solution_en:
The most appropriate phrasal verb to fill in the blank is 'ironed out'. The phrasal verb "ironed out" means to resolve or eliminate problems, issues, or difficulties in a situation. In the context of the sentence, it implies that the driver skilfully handled the situation, smoothing over any potential consequences or complications related to the traffic violation. The other options do not use the appropriate preposition for the given context. Hence, (c) is the correct answer.

NOTE:

Phrasal verb: A phrase that consists of a verb with a preposition or adverb or both, the meaning of which is different from the meaning of its separate parts. Example: She has always looked down on me. Here, the phrasal verb 'to look down on someone' doesn't mean that you are looking down from a higher place at someone who is below you; it means that you think that you are better than someone.

A Preposition is a word placed before a noun or a pronoun or a noun equivalent (pronoun, adverb, gerund, infinitive, adverbial clause, or any clause that can be used as the object of the preposition) and shows a relationship in space or time or a logical relationship between two or more people, places, or things in a sentence.

Examples:

1) The teacher scolded the child on being late.

2) We're going to a party.
